q: Copper(II) oxide is heated with hydrogen: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. Which statement is correct?
options: Hydrogen is reduced because it gains oxygen
Copper(II) oxide is reduced because it gains oxygen
Copper(II) oxide is oxidised because it loses oxygen
Copper(II) oxide is reduced because it loses oxygen
explain: CuO loses oxygen to form Cu so it is reduced. Hydrogen gains oxygen to form water so it is oxidised.

q: Magnesium burns in oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Which statement is correct?
options: Oxygen is oxidised because it gains magnesium
Magnesium is reduced because it loses oxygen
Magnesium is reduced because it gains oxygen
Magnesium is oxidised because it gains oxygen
explain: Magnesium gains oxygen and is oxidised. A gain of oxygen is oxidation.

q: Which equation represents a redox reaction?
options: HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l)
CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g)
2CuO(s) + C(s) → 2Cu(s) + CO₂(g)
CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq)
explain: In 2CuO + C → 2Cu + CO₂, CuO loses oxygen (reduced) and carbon gains oxygen (oxidised). The other equations involve no gain or loss of oxygen.

q: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, which statement is correct?
options: Iron(III) oxide is reduced and carbon monoxide is oxidised
Both are oxidised
Iron(III) oxide is oxidised and carbon monoxide is reduced
Both are reduced
explain: Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen so it is reduced, while CO gains oxygen to become CO₂ so it is oxidised.

q: In the reaction 2Mg + CO₂ → 2MgO + C, which row is correct?
options: Mg | CO₂
C | MgO
CO₂ | Mg
Mg | MgO
explain: Magnesium gains oxygen so it is oxidised, and carbon dioxide loses oxygen so it is reduced.

q: Iron rusts when it reacts with oxygen and water. In terms of oxygen, what happens to the iron?
options: It is oxidised because it loses oxygen
It is reduced because it loses oxygen
It is oxidised because it gains oxygen
It is reduced because it gains oxygen
explain: Rust is a compound of iron with oxygen, so the iron has gained oxygen and been oxidised.

q: Black copper(II) oxide is heated with carbon and a pink-brown solid forms. What does this show?
options: The change is a physical change
Copper has been oxidised to copper(II) oxide
Carbon has been reduced
Copper(II) oxide has been reduced to copper
explain: Loss of oxygen from copper(II) oxide to give copper is reduction.

q: Which reaction involves the reduction of a metal oxide?
options: Heating copper in air to make copper(II) oxide
Heating iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide to make iron
Burning magnesium in air
Rusting of iron in damp air
explain: Iron(III) oxide loses oxygen to carbon monoxide, so it is reduced. Copper and magnesium gain oxygen, and rusting is oxidation.

q: Which row correctly links the change with its name?
options: Gain of oxygen | reduction
Loss of oxygen | oxidation
Gain of oxygen | oxidation
Loss of oxygen | neutralisation
explain: Gain of oxygen is oxidation and loss of oxygen is reduction.

q: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe, which statement is correct?
options: Aluminium is reduced and iron(III) oxide is oxidised
Neither is oxidised or reduced
Both are oxidised
Aluminium is oxidised and iron(III) oxide is reduced
explain: Aluminium gains oxygen to form Al₂O₃ (oxidation). Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen to form iron (reduction).

q: Which row correctly defines oxidation and reduction?
options: decrease in oxidation number | increase in oxidation number
loss of electrons | gain of electrons
decrease in oxidation number | gain of electrons
gain of electrons | loss of electrons
explain: Oxidation is loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation number. Reduction is gain of electrons or a decrease in oxidation number.

q: The change Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ takes place. Which statement is correct?
options: It is oxidation because electrons are lost
It is reduction because electrons are lost
It is oxidation because electrons are gained
It is reduction because electrons are gained
explain: The iron ion loses an electron and its oxidation number rises from +2 to +3, which is oxidation.

q: The change Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻ takes place. Which statement is correct?
options: It is oxidation because electrons are gained
It is reduction because electrons are gained
It is oxidation because chlorine gains oxygen
It is reduction because electrons are lost
explain: Chlorine gains electrons and its oxidation number falls from 0 to −1, which is reduction.

q: What is the oxidation number of sulfur in the sulfate ion, SO₄²⁻?
explain: Each oxygen is −2, so S + 4(−2) = −2. Therefore S = +6.

q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in the manganate(VII) ion, MnO₄⁻?
Which species contains nitrogen with an oxidation number of +5?
options: NO₃⁻
NH₃
NO₂
N₂O
explain: In NO₃⁻, N + 3(−2) = −1, so N = +5. NO₂ is +4, NH₃ is −3 and N₂O is +1.

q: Zinc is added to copper(II) sulfate solution: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Which change in oxidation number happens?
options: Zinc goes from 0 to +2, so zinc is oxidised
Copper goes from 0 to +2, so copper is oxidised
Zinc goes from +2 to 0, so zinc is oxidised
Zinc goes from 0 to +2, so zinc is reduced
explain: Zinc atoms (0) become Zn²⁺ (+2), so the oxidation number increases and zinc is oxidised. Copper goes from +2 to 0 and is reduced.

q: Which reaction is NOT a redox reaction?
options: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O
Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu
explain: In the CuO and acid reaction every oxidation number stays the same (Cu +2, O −2, H +1, S +6). The other reactions all include an element changing its oxidation number.

q: Which change is a reduction?
options: Cr in Cr₂O₇²⁻ changing to Cr³⁺
Sulfur in SO₂ changing to sulfur in SO₄²⁻
Cu changing to Cu²⁺
Fe²⁺ changing to Fe³⁺
explain: Chromium goes from +6 to +3, a decrease in oxidation number. The other changes all show an increase in oxidation number.

q: Acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution is added to a solution of a reducing agent. What colour change is seen?
options: Orange to green
Purple to brown
Purple to colourless
Colourless to purple
explain: Purple manganate(VII) is reduced to almost colourless Mn²⁺ by a reducing agent.

q: Aqueous potassium iodide is added to a solution of an oxidising agent. What colour change shows that a redox reaction has taken place?
options: Colourless to purple
Colourless to brown
Brown to colourless
Colourless to blue
explain: Iodide ions are oxidised to iodine, which makes the solution brown.

q: Which is the correct definition of an oxidising agent?
options: A substance that oxidises another substance and is itself reduced
A substance that reduces another substance and is itself reduced
A substance that oxidises another substance and is itself oxidised
A substance that reduces another substance and is itself oxidised
explain: An oxidising agent takes electrons from another substance, which is oxidised, and is itself reduced.

q: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, which is the reducing agent?
options: Fe₂O₃
CO₂
CO
Fe
explain: CO takes oxygen from the iron(III) oxide and is itself oxidised to CO₂, so it is the reducing agent.

q: In the reaction Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂, which is the oxidising agent?
options: KCl
Br₂
KBr
Cl₂
explain: Chlorine gains electrons (0 to −1) and is reduced, so it oxidises the bromide ions and is the oxidising agent.

q: Magnesium reacts with dilute acid: Mg + 2H⁺ → Mg²⁺ + H₂. Which statement is correct?
options: H⁺ is the oxidising agent because it gains electrons
H⁺ is the reducing agent because it gains electrons
Mg²⁺ is reduced because it gains electrons
Mg is the oxidising agent because it loses electrons
explain: Mg loses electrons (oxidised, reducing agent). H⁺ gains electrons (reduced) so it is the oxidising agent.

q: Acidified potassium manganate(VII) is decolourised by a solution of iron(II) sulfate. Which statement is correct?
options: Fe²⁺ is oxidised to Fe³⁺, so iron(II) sulfate is acting as a reducing agent
Manganate(VII) is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent
Fe²⁺ is reduced to Fe³⁺, so iron(II) sulfate is acting as a reducing agent
Fe²⁺ is oxidised to Fe³⁺, so iron(II) sulfate is acting as an oxidising agent
explain: Loss of purple colour shows the manganate(VII) has been reduced. Fe²⁺ loses electrons, so it is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent.

q: In the reaction 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O, which statement about sulfur is correct?
options: Sulfur is neither oxidised nor reduced
Sulfur is reduced only
Sulfur is both oxidised and reduced
Sulfur is oxidised only
explain: Sulfur in H₂S goes from −2 to 0 (oxidised) and sulfur in SO₂ goes from +4 to 0 (reduced).

q: Which row gives the correct oxidation number?
options: Cl in ClO₃⁻ | +3
Cr in Cr₂O₇²⁻ | +6
S in SO₂ | +2
N in NH₄⁺ | +4
explain: In Cr₂O₇²⁻, 2Cr + 7(−2) = −2, so Cr = +6. S in SO₂ is +4, Cl in ClO₃⁻ is +5 and N in NH₄⁺ is −3.

q: A reaction takes 20 s at 40 °C and 80 s at 20 °C, with all other conditions the same. What does this show?
options: The reaction is faster at the higher temperature
A catalyst is present at 20 °C
Temperature has no effect on the rate
The reaction is faster at the lower temperature
explain: A shorter time for the same change means a faster rate, so raising the temperature increased the rate.

q: Which two colours are shown by cobalt(II) chloride when it is anhydrous and when it is hydrated?
options: Blue when anhydrous and white when hydrated
Blue when anhydrous and pink when hydrated
Pink when anhydrous and blue when hydrated
White when anhydrous and blue when hydrated
explain: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue and it turns pink when it takes in water to become hydrated.
